title: PDF Solutions CONNECT 2026: Where Semiconductor Data Meets AI - Semiwiki
gist: A preview of PDF Solutions CONNECT 2026 (October 15-16, Westin St. Francis, San Francisco) that doubles as a thesis: semiconductor manufacturing leadership will hinge on converting scattered fab data into trusted decisions, and the company's new AI-first Exensio Aurora architecture is pitched as petabyte-scale, agentic-AI-ready infrastructure for that shift.

themes.theme: Data-to-decision as the new manufacturing edge

insights.claim: Semiconductor manufacturing leadership will depend not on producing more data but on turning that data into timely, trustworthy decisions.
insights.so_what: Reframes fab competitiveness as an analytics-software problem, expanding the addressable market for yield and data platform vendors.
insights.quote: manufacturing leadership will depend not simply on producing more data, but on turning that data into timely, trustworthy decisions
insights.locator: The semiconductor industry is entering a period
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Semiconductor companies do not suffer from a shortage of information; their difficulty is connecting information scattered across equipment sensors, process recipes, metrology systems, manufacturing execution systems, engineering reports and expert knowledge.
insights.so_what: Integration, not collection, is where spend goes — favors vendors that own cross-system data plumbing over point-tool analytics.
insights.locator: That focus matters because semiconductor companies
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: As devices and fabrication processes become more sophisticated, an engineer may need to investigate several systems before understanding a yield, quality or equipment-performance change, and every delay between detecting a problem and identifying its cause affects production costs, delivery schedules and customer commitments.
insights.so_what: Quantifies the ROI pitch — time-to-root-cause maps directly to cost and on-time delivery, the metrics fabs will pay to improve.
insights.locator: As devices and fabrication processes become more sophisticated
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

themes.theme: Exensio Aurora and agentic AI in the fab

insights.claim: Exensio Aurora is PDF Solutions' new AI-first architecture for its Exensio Analytics platform, built to analyze semiconductor manufacturing data at petabyte scale and to support secure use of agentic AI across manufacturing operations and the supply chain.
insights.so_what: A named product cycle to track — agentic AI moving into production fab workflows is a new software attach point on semiconductor capex.
insights.locator: A central focus will be Exensio Aurora
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Planned demonstrations cover large language model-driven analytics, StudioAI and a new user experience, with technical sessions on the underlying platform architecture.
insights.so_what: LLM-driven analytics reaching demo stage in fab tooling is an early indicator of where EDA/manufacturing software pricing power moves next.
insights.locator: Attendees will be able to explore demonstrations
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: A generic AI model may recognize patterns without understanding how products, processes, tools and test results relate to one another, so AI only shortens time-to-root-cause when it operates on reliable data with the correct manufacturing context.
insights.so_what: Domain-contextualized data is the moat against horizontal AI vendors entering fab analytics — a defensibility argument for specialists.
insights.quote: A generic model may recognize patterns without understanding how products, processes, tools and test results relate to one another.
insights.locator: AI can help shorten that interval
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Semiconductor manufacturers require explainability, repeatability, security, governance and human oversight before AI-generated recommendations can influence production.
insights.so_what: These gating requirements explain why fab AI adoption lags consumer AI — governance features, not model quality, set the deployment pace.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: The industry is transitioning from isolated AI projects toward connected, governed systems capable of supporting complete engineering workflows, with predictive maintenance, anomaly detection and root-cause analysis gaining value when insights flow into coordinated action.
insights.so_what: Platform consolidation over point solutions — a pattern that historically drives M&A among smaller fab-analytics vendors.
insights.locator: The event also reflects a broader transition
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: AI in semiconductor manufacturing is emerging not as a replacement for engineers or established process-control tools, but as a way to make expertise more accessible, accelerate investigations and orchestrate work across systems.
insights.so_what: Tempers headcount-reduction narratives around industrial AI; the value accrues as throughput per engineer, not layoffs.
insights.locator: AI is therefore emerging not as a replacement
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: PDF Solutions CONNECT 2026 runs October 15-16, 2026 at the Westin St. Francis on Union Square in San Francisco, combining executive and technical keynotes, customer presentations, panels, live demonstrations, workshops and direct access to product managers and developers.
insights.so_what: A dated catalyst where Aurora customer proof points and adoption commentary are likely to surface.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Announced speakers include PDF Solutions co-founder and CEO John Kibarian, Bloomberg Technology executive producer Emily Chang and energy and technology expert Dr. Jonathan Koomey, plus speakers from Samsung, Intel, Qualcomm, POET and STMicroelectronics.
insights.so_what: The customer roster is the real signal — Samsung, Intel and Qualcomm presenting suggests platform traction at leading-edge accounts.
insights.locator: Announced speakers include PDF Solutions co-founder
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

themes.theme: Why fab analytics matters beyond the factory

insights.claim: Improvements in yield, quality, reliability and equipment productivity influence the cost and availability of chips used in vehicles, data centers, communications networks and consumer products.
insights.so_what: Positions fab analytics as an upstream lever on downstream chip supply and pricing across end markets.
insights.locator: Bottom line: PDF Solutions CONNECT 2026 matters
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Analytics solutions in semiconductors must work across long equipment lifecycles, proprietary systems, different data formats and geographically dispersed partners, which is why practitioner exchange at events carries unusual weight.
insights.so_what: High switching costs and integration depth argue for durable revenue at incumbent fab-analytics vendors.
insights.locator: That exchange is especially valuable in semiconductors
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
